# Facilitation Architecture Rules

<!-- Generated by packages/rules/generate.mjs from data/laws/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

The exercises come from public facilitation practice: the design-sprint tradition, Liberating Structures by Henri Lipmanowicz and Keith McCandless, Lean and Scrum lineage, and methods the field has used long enough that no single author is documented. Each card names an origin where one is documented and says plainly where none is.
Every card answers the four questions a facilitator has in the room - how many, how long, how hard, what we leave with - then the steps, then the failure that usually arrives.

## Alignment & Framing

### WS-01 — Problem Framing Canvas

**Deliverable.** A bounded problem statement with the user impact and the business cost written down.

**At a glance.** 5–15 people · 45–60 min · intermediate

**When it goes wrong.** Solution jumping: the statement names the fix the room already wanted, so the session debates a tool.

**The fix.** Strip the tool out of the sentence. Ask what happens in the workflow that costs measurable time or money; rewrite it without naming a product.

**Provenance.** Source protocol: the steps follow the written script in the source.
